notices.short_title: Consultant Services, Coney Island Boardwalk Reconstruction
notices.description:
The New York City Economic Development Corporation (NYCEDC) is seeking a consultant team to provide Progressive Design-Build services for the integrated delivery of the design and reconstruction of the Coney Island Riegelmann Boardwalk (the Project). The Coney Island Riegelmann Boardwalk (Boardwalk) is located between W 37th Street on its west end and Brighton 15th Street on its east end in Brooklyn along the southern shore of the Coney Island peninsula. It is located on property under the jurisdiction of the NYC Department of Parks & Recreation (NYC Parks) and is maintained and operated by NYC Parks.

The Project will consist of the reconstruction of the 2.4-mile Boardwalk structure in its entirety, including piles, piles caps, and the decking system, and will be designed to improve climate and storm resiliency in the area by elevating portions of the boardwalk to approximately +16 NAVD88, including protective barriers in the subgrade. The Project will also include: topside amenities including site furnishings, lighting, fencing/railings, public access stairs/ramps and street end plazas; utilities, including but not limited to drainage, water service, and electrical; renov…
notices.plain: The Economic Development Corporation is seeking consultant teams, chosen by Request for Qualifications with responses due Nov. 4, 2026, to design and rebuild the 2.4-mile Coney Island Riegelmann Boardwalk in Brooklyn, which NYC Parks owns and maintains.

notices.short_title: Bronx NAQE- Catholic Charities- Construction Site Safety Training
notices.description:
The NYC Department of Small Business Services is entering into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension Contract with Catholic Charities Community Services Archdiocese of NY, to provide site safety training in the borough of the Bronx. Local Law 196 (2017) establishes Site Safety Training requirements for workers at most construction sites in the City of New York. Local Law 196 also requires that an agency designated by the Mayor will develop a program to provide equal access to the training required by Section 3321 of the New York City Building Code. The New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) has been designated to provide such a training program and to ensure that these essential safety standards are in place to protect the lives of construction workers and the public consistent with the requirements outlined in the local law. The contract term will be from 7/1/2026 to 6/30/2027, in the amount of $347,034.00

Vendors interested in responding to this or other future solicitations for these types of services should contact Marielis Martinez at procurementhelpdesk@sbs.nyc.gov.

notices.short_title: NOTICE OF FILING - 43-58 11TH STREET, QUEENS
notices.description:
NOTICE OF FILING

Pursuant to §1731 of the New York Public Authorities Law, notice has been filed for the proposed site selection of all or portions of Block 453, Lot 1 and any other property in the immediate vicinity which may be necessary for the proposed construction of a new, approximately 972-seat intermediate school in Queens.

The proposed site is located at 43-58 11th Street on the north side of 44th Avenue, between 10th Street and 11th Street in the Long Island City neighborhood of Queens. The site is currently occupied by one to two-story commercial and manufacturing buildings. The proposed site to be acquired by the New York City School Construction Authority, on behalf of the New York City Department of Education, is an approximately 47,255 square foot (1.08 acre) lot.

notable.short_title: Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) - 5-Year Review - Notice of Intent to Request the Release of Funds
notable.description:
COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT (CDBG)

ALTERNATIVE ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM (AEP) 5-YEAR REVIEW - 2026

NOTICE OF INTENT TO REQUEST RELEASE OF FUNDS (NOI RROF)

             

REQUEST FOR RELEASE OF FUNDS

On or about October 8, 2026, the City of New York (the City) anticipates submitting a request to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) for the release of $51,780,000 of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) funds authorized under the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992, to undertake the Citys Demolition Program citywide, for a period of five years.

The Alternative Enforcement Program (AEP) is intended to address the serious physical deterioration of the most distressed buildings in New York City. Through AEP, the NYC Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) can order the property owner to repair or replace building systems as well as to address violations. Using criteria set forth in the City's Administrative Code, HPD annually designates 250 multiple dwellings that are high consumers of…
notable.plain: The Office of Management and Budget plans to ask the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development to release $51,780,000 in Community Development Block Grant funds for the citywide Demolition Program over five years.

notable.description: COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. notable.short_title: Bronx NAQE- Catholic Charities- Construction Site Safety Training
notable.description:
The NYC Department of Small Business Services is entering into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension Contract with Catholic Charities Community Services Archdiocese of NY, to provide site safety training in the borough of the Bronx. Local Law 196 (2017) establishes Site Safety Training requirements for workers at most construction sites in the City of New York. Local Law 196 also requires that an agency designated by the Mayor will develop a program to provide equal access to the training required by Section 3321 of the New York City Building Code. The New York City Department of Small Business Services (SBS) has been designated to provide such a training program and to ensure that these essential safety standards are in place to protect the lives of construction workers and the public consistent with the requirements outlined in the local law. The contract term will be from 7/1/2026 to 6/30/2027, in the amount of $347,034.00

Vendors interested in responding to this or other future solicitations for these types of services should contact Marielis Martinez at procurementhelpdesk@sbs.nyc.gov.
notable.plain: The Department of Small Business Services intends to extend its Negotiated Acquisition contract with Catholic Charities Community Services Archdiocese of NY for construction site safety training in the Bronx, for $347,034 over July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027.
